title: Biblical Passage Fragments — Observer / Stewardship / Recurrence + Operator Wave 22
translation: World English Bible (WEB) for quoted entries; Project paraphrase for added operator entries
license: WEB public domain; project paraphrases are original summaries

fragments.text: After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven; and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, was one saying, ‘Come up here, and I will show you the things which must happen after this.’
Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done. I say: My counsel will stand, and I will do all that I please.

Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven. Therefore, when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself … so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

Who then is Apollos, and who is Paul, but servants through whom you believed, and each as the Lord gave to him? I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase. So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.
As therefore you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, even as you were taught, abounding in it in thanksgiving.
Parental imagery joins carrying, healing, feeding, easing burden and teaching a child to walk.
Eagle imagery combines stirring the nest, hovering, catching and carrying the young.
Access to God is described as a new and living way associated with Christ's flesh/body.
Through Christ there is access in one Spirit to Father; people become household and joined dwelling.
The Branch/sprout grows, builds the temple, bears honor and rules from a throne.
The body is joined through supporting connections; each part contributes and the body grows.
Jesus contrasts rule-by-domination with greatness expressed through service.
Teacher/Lord status is enacted through foot-washing service and offered as an example to imitate.
Greater knowledge and entrustment bring greater accountability.
One body has many members with distinct functions and mutual dependence.
Living stones are built together into a spiritual house.
Leadership gifts equip other members for ministry and build the body toward maturity.
A gardener asks for more time, cultivates the soil and tests whether a fruit tree will become fruitful.
Solomon dedicates the temple while stressing that the divine source cannot be contained by the building.
Creator and presence are described as exceeding human-made temples while creatures live and move in relation to God.
A divine encounter is mediated through bush and fire imagery while the material sign remains distinguishable from the source.
Spirit, adoption, children, inheritance and address to Father are joined in one relational sequence.
Strong rule is immediately paired with shepherd imagery: gathering, carrying lambs and gentle leading.
The judgment scene turns on feeding, welcoming, clothing, visiting and treatment of vulnerable people.
Parental discipline is framed as difficult formation whose stated outcome is later peaceful fruit.
New wine and old wineskins illustrate that changed content or process may require a fitting container.
Moses asks for a fuller encounter but receives a constrained, protected view rather than unrestricted access.
Present knowledge and seeing are described as partial, with mirror imagery contrasting incomplete perception with fuller knowing.
